column1: # Mutant batch for issue #38's snippet picker.
#   scripts/mutate.sh batch scripts/mutants/snip-picker.tsv
# Tab-separated: NAME <TAB> FILE <TAB> FROM <TAB> TO [<TAB> TEST_FILTER]
# FROM must occur EXACTLY ONCE in FILE or the mutant is refused.
# 🔴 DEFINITIONS ONLY, NEVER RESULTS. A verdict is void the moment the
# tree moves — see scripts/MUTATION-TESTING.md. The verdicts these produced
# live in the pull request for #38, stamped with the commit they were measured
# on.
# 🔴 WHY THIS BATCH EXISTS AT ALL. None of #38's tests is a regression
# test: every class it touches arrives with the feature, so "red at the base
# commit" would be a compile error rather than a guard watched failing. This
# batch is what stands in for that — each row breaks ONE expression and names
# the class whose OWN assertion must go red, so a kill is attributable to that
# expression and is credited to the guard that actually executed.
# Each TEST_FILTER is the single class making the claim, which is deliberate:
# it both shortens the run and makes the kill a statement about that class
# rather than about whatever else happened to notice. A filter is only safe
# because the harness refuses a run that executed zero tests — without that,
# a typo'd filter reads as SURVIVED.
# Every mutant leaves the branch structure intact. The two that replace a
# statement with `Unit` (m-snip10, m-snip16) remove a guard or a write WITHOUT
# touching its enclosing condition, which is the isolation
# scripts/MUTATION-TESTING.md requires: a mutant that deletes the condition
# too proves nothing about the guard and dies for the wrong reason.
